purpose: Explain a rally as opponent state, a possible purpose of the shot, the available replies, and the next observed choice.
authority_limit: These are conditional coaching interpretations supported by published sources. They are not measurements of a player's intention or proof of national-team coaching expertise.

inferred: current shot destination from the next receiver contact
observation_contract.unknown_rule: If contact, identity, court mapping or the relevant next contact is uncertain, omit that claim instead of completing the sequence from alternation.
observation_contract.causality_rule: A later movement is an observed response, not proof that the preceding shot caused it or that the hitter planned it.
observation_contract.wording_zh: 用“像是想”“可以理解为”“接下来要看”，不用“她早就算准”“必然”“百分之百”。

prediction_contract.cutoff: The prediction is made at the current contact, using observations available at or before that contact.
forbidden_inputs: shot_family inferred from the next contact
prediction_contract.retrospective_note: A destination inferred using the next contact may explain an observed sequence retrospectively, but is not eligible as an input to a prospective next-reply prediction.
prediction_contract.evaluation: Freeze rules before the held-out rallies. Report coverage, sample size, prediction-set size and accuracy beside a development-set majority baseline of the same set size. Unknowns are not wins.
prediction_contract.baseline_limit: Do not learn the majority reply or tune thresholds from the held-out rallies.

rules.opponent_state: The opponent has been displaced toward the rear and has not yet recovered forward.
rules.choice: Consider the available front-court space rather than repeating an unpressured deep shot.
rules.expected_reply: The opponent must travel forward if the next shot is genuinely short. An early arrival can still produce an attacking net reply; a late arrival may constrain the reply.
rules.check: Show the opponent's position before the choice and where the opponent actually next contacts. Check the travel and contact state, not an untracked landing.
required_evidence: two verified contacts in one continuous rally
both players' court positions at the choice
do_not_apply: the opponent is already moving forward
the current shot destination is unknown
rules.source_limit: Two authored works support the tactical aim, not a probability that this opponent will lose the rally.

rules.opponent_state: The opponent is reaching or arriving at the front court, leaving distance to cover behind.
rules.choice: A deep reply can make the opponent reverse the frontward movement, if the hitter has the time and control to play it.
rules.expected_reply: The opponent may retreat for an overhead reply. A short or loose deep shot can instead give the opponent an attack.
rules.check: Show the initial forward displacement, the reversal and the next contact depth. Do not equate any backward step with a successful tactical trap.
do_not_apply: pose jitter is larger than the apparent reversal
rules.source_limit: The space is created by the opponent's displacement, not by the label of the shot alone.

rules.opponent_state: The hitter is late or stretched while the opponent is better positioned to continue attacking.
rules.choice: A sufficiently high, deep defensive reply can buy recovery time instead of forcing an immediate winner attempt.
rules.expected_reply: The opponent receives farther back while the hitter gets time to recover. A short reply can still be attacked; deep does not mean safe.
rules.check: Compare the hitter's position at this contact with the position before the following opponent contact. Show whether recovery actually occurred.
do_not_apply: unseen flight described as a measured high clear
source_lineage: Jingyi Shannon Chia, 2018, explicitly citing Downey 2007 for the recovery tactic
蕭博仁, 2005, observed elite women's singles patterns
rules.source_limit: One source gives the strategic rationale; the other describes a specific player's defensive pattern. Neither makes this the correct choice in every situation.

rules.title_zh: 接得越低，下一拍越要看清
rules.opponent_state: The receiver is late near the net and cannot attack above the net.
rules.choice: A tight short shot can make an upward reply more attractive, but the hitter must still cover a net return.
rules.expected_reply: Possible replies include a lift, a net return and a cross-court net reply. Do not declare a lift inevitable.
rules.check: Pause before the receiver contacts, name the competing replies, then play the actual next contact and identify what happened only if visible.
required_evidence: receiver's visible contact state near the net
enough image detail to distinguish low from high contact
do_not_apply: the net shot sits up for a kill
a family label is inferred only from elapsed time
source_lineage: Julie K'Bidy, 2021, recorded expert-coach dialogue with multiple reply options
rules.source_limit: The coaching aim and the available alternatives are both retained. An intended weak lift is not an observed weak lift.

rules.opponent_state: After a short defensive reply, the opponent can answer quickly at the net or play a slower lift.
rules.choice: Recovery can favor the urgent front-court threat while retaining the ability to retreat, instead of always returning to one geometric center.
rules.expected_reply: A quick straight net reply is the immediate threat in the cited drill. A lift remains possible and must be allowed for.
rules.check: Show where the player waits, what the opponent actually replies and whether that waiting position helps with the response. Do not call a habitual median position universally optimal.
do_not_apply: the opponent has a different attacking option
a fixed central base is used as a correctness target
source_lineage: Julie K'Bidy, 2021, expert-coach and player dialogue
Jingyi Shannon Chia, 2018, discussion of opponent-relative base position, citing Mack 2016
rules.source_limit: The source records disagreement from the player, and the coach then adds the lift option. This is a contextual tradeoff, not a universal instruction to stand forward.

rules.opponent_state: The opponent has visibly committed movement toward an expected reply or has been displaced by the previous shot.
rules.choice: An available opposite-direction reply may make that movement costly. A cross-court shot is not automatically better, since it can travel farther and allow more time.
rules.expected_reply: The opponent may have to brake or reverse. If the opponent was not committed, the same shot may create no advantage.
rules.check: Show the motion before contact and the observed movement after it. Use a direction change as evidence; do not infer deception or intention from position alone.
do_not_apply: movement vector is dominated by noise
unseen shuttle direction is drawn as a tracked path
source_lineage: Virginia Hicks, 1973, conditional cross-court serve return
Julie K'Bidy, 2021, coach prioritizing speed opposite a displaced opponent
rules.source_limit: The two contexts differ. They support reading committed movement, not prescribing the same cross-court shot for every rally.

interpretation_guard.text_zh: 同一个动作，不一定是同一个目的。先看双方的位置、来球和前一拍，再说这一拍可能在争什么。
interpretation_guard.meaning: The same stroke can attack, neutralize pressure or conserve effort. Placement and speed matter through their effect on this opponent in this rally.
